function.description:
A powerful search tool built on ripgrep.

Usage:
  - ALWAYS use `grep` for search tasks. NEVER invoke `grep`/`rg` as a `run_bash` command — `grep` is optimised for sandbox-correct access.
  - Supports full ripgrep regex (e.g., "log.*Error", "function\\s+\\w+"). Literal braces need escaping: `interface\\{\\}` finds `interface{}` in Go code.
  - Filter files with `glob` (e.g., "*.py", "*.{ts,tsx}") or `type` (e.g., "py", "rust"); narrow `path` to a directory.
  - Output modes: "content" shows matching lines (supports `context=N` and `-n` line numbers), "files_with_matches" shows only file paths (default), "count" shows per-file match counts.
  - When the issue text doesn't name a file or you're unsure which file to edit, use `grep(pattern='<keyword>', output_mode='files_with_matches')` first to locate the buggy file; then `read_file` it.
  - Use `output_mode='content'` with `context=N` to see surrounding lines.
  - Pass `-i=true` for case-insensitive search (useful for case-sensitivity bugs — try searching the lowercase form first).
  - Use `head_limit=N` to cap large result sets; the tool reports `applied_limit` when truncated so you can paginate with `offset`/`head_limit`.
  - Multiline patterns need `multiline=true` (e.g., `struct \\{\\[\\s\\S]*?field`).

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to repo root.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g., "*.py", "*.{ts,tsx}") — maps to rg --glob.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: py, js, rust, go, java.

output_mode.description: Output mode. "content" shows matching lines (supports context=N, -n line numbers). "files_with_matches" shows file paths only (default, best for locating). "count" shows per-file match counts.
